case_title: Sarabjeet Singh Mokha v. District Magistrate, Jabalpur & Ors.
previous_criminal_record: Yes - detention grounds cite a 2004 Gorakhpur case (acquitted); antecedents are an allegation in the grounds, not a court finding
statutory_provisions: NSA s.3(2) (detention order). Underlying FIR cited: IPC ss.274, 275, 308, 420, 120B; Disaster Management Act s.53; Epidemic Diseases Act s.3
evidence_type: Not assessed by the Court; detention grounds relied on Section 161 CrPC statements of co-accused and another person, and newspaper reports
trial_court_outcome: Not applicable - no criminal trial; District Magistrate passed three-month preventive detention order on 11 May 2021
high_court_outcome: Writ petition under Article 226 dismissed (24 August 2021)
neutral_facts: The accused, who ran a hospital, is alleged to have, in connivance with others, procured fake Remdesivir injections which were administered to Covid-19 patients during the pandemic in order to make illegal profits. An FIR was registered at a Jabalpur police station under provisions of the Indian Penal Code, the Disaster Management Act and the Epidemic Diseases Act. Investigation included a matter in Gujarat in which fake Remdesivir injections were reportedly seized from a manufacturing unit. In a statement recorded under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, a co-accused who ran the hospital pharmacy stated that the accused had procured the injections without a bill. Another person stated that the accused's son had asked him to send the injections from Indore to Jabalpur, and that he had been made to speak to the accused about it. The injections were said to have been transported by a travel company and received at Jabalpur by the co-accused on behalf of the accused. They were stated to have been administered to 50 patients at the hospital on a particular date. The detention grounds stated that several patients had died after receiving spurious injections and that the incident had been reported in newspapers, causing public outcry. Records alleged that 500 such injections, worth Rs.15 lakhs, had been ordered by the accused through fake bills from a manufacturer in Gujarat. A police request for preventive action followed, reiterating these allegations.
physical_harm: Alleged in detention grounds: several untimely deaths and casualties among patients; not a court finding
number_of_offences: Not applicable - no criminal charge tried; preventive detention under NSA s.3(2)
financial_property_loss: Alleged procurement of 500 injections worth Rs.15 lakhs (allegation only)
key_evidence_accepted: None on the merits; the Court decided on procedural grounds (delay in deciding representation and failure to communicate rejection) and did not examine the detention grounds
custody_duration: Detained from 12 May 2021; detention extended, with the extended period running to 12 February 2022
trial_duration: offence: 30 April 2021 (alleged administration of injections); trial judgment: not applicable (no trial); High Court: 24 August 2021; Supreme Court: 29 October 2021
legal_representation: Appellant: Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv., with Ashwani Kumar Dubey and others. Respondents: Saurabh Mishra, AAG, with Ms. Ankita Choudhary, Dy. AG, and Sunny Choudhary
investigation_status: FIR registered 10 May 2021; appellant arrested 26 May 2021; final report under s.173 CrPC submitted 6 August 2021
procedural_irregularity: Unexplained delay of about 60 days by the State Government in deciding the representation dated 18 May 2021; Central Government's rejection (24 June 2021) not shown to have been communicated to the detenu; no reasons given for failure to communicate
appeal_history: Trial court: not applicable (no trial; detention order by District Magistrate). High Court: writ petition dismissed 24 August 2021. Supreme Court: appeal allowed; detention order and extensions quashed
prosecution_argument: No unreasonable delay in considering the representation; State awaited Advisory Board report; representation rejected after Advisory Board; rejection duly communicated; subjective satisfaction not justiciable; solitary act sufficient; grounds severable under s.5A
defence_argument: Representation not timely considered or decided; State rejection not furnished to detenu; Central rejection never received; approval and rejection not communicated forthwith; stale antecedents, media-outrage grounds, and extensions unjustified
legal_principle_applied: Art.22(4)-(5) and s.8(1) NSA require prompt communication of grounds and expeditious consideration of the representation by the appropriate government, independent of the Advisory Board; unexplained delay and failure to communicate the rejection vitiate the detention
precedent_relied_upon: Followed: Jayanarayan Sukul (1970) 1 SCC 219; Haradhan Saha (1975) 3 SCC 198; K.M. Abdulla Kunhi (1991) 1 SCC 476. Relied on: Frances Coralie Mullin (1980) 2 SCC 275; Harish Pahwa (1981) 2 SCC 710; Mohinuddin (1987) 4 SCC 58; Ankit Ashok Jalan (2020) 16 SCC 127; Haji Mohd. Akhlaq 1988 Supp SCC 538; State of Punjab v. Sukhpal Singh (1990) 1 SCC 35; Madan Lal Anand (1990) 1 SCC 81. Distinguished: Union of India v. Saleena (2016) 3 SCC 437
other_sentence_order: Impugned High Court judgment set aside; detention order dated 11 May 2021 and extensions dated 15 July 2021 and 30 September 2021 quashed and set aside
